newsitem.title: BULGARIA: South Korea's Daewoo eyes Bulgaria's Balkanbank.
newsitem.headline: South Korea's Daewoo eyes Bulgaria's Balkanbank.

text.p: South Korean concern Daewoo Corp said on Thursday it was considering buying Bulgaria's ailing Balkanbank to service the company's expansion in this debt-ridden Balkan country.
"We would like to have a Bulgarian registered bank... because of our expanded activities here," Daewoo Sofia branch office representative Chung-Hwan Kim told a news conference.
"We discussed the matter with (Bulgaria's) cabinet and they recommended to us Balkanbank," said Chung-Hwan Kim.
Balkanbank is one of nine local commercial banks placed under special supervision last month in a bid to stabilise the country's crumbling financial system.
After reviewing the banks' financial state, the central bank is expected to decide for which of them to seek insolvency through courts and which to stabilise and offer to investors.
Of the nine banks, Balkanbank has the highest level of personal and company deposits and it posted a cumulative loss of 9.3 billion levs up to the end of August this year, a bank report showed.
Balkanbank's capital to risk assets ratio stood at minus 37.7 percent, a long way from the Basle banking standards of plus eight percent.
"Our experts are currently reviewing the documents of Balkanbank and we are waiting for their decision," said Chung-Hwan Kim.
He added that Daewoo had submitted a letter of intent to Bulgaria's central bank expressing interest in Balkanbank.
"We are studying not only the Balkanbank option but also other Bulgarian banks," he said.

Daewoo said it was also interested in Bulgaria's plans for a partial sale of its state-owned telecommunication company and announced intentions to bid for a second GSM operator contract in Bulgaria. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
